identity.title: Radial pulse irregularly irregular on palpation (>=20-30 s)

technique.how: Palpate the radial pulse with two fingers for at least 20-30 s (a full 60 s if any irregularity is suspected). Classify as regular, regularly irregular (a repeating pattern, e.g. bigeminy or dropped beats), or irregularly irregular (no pattern in timing or volume). If irregular, obtain a 12-lead ECG; an apical-radial deficit supports atrial fibrillation.
technique.prerequisites: Patient at rest; count long enough to catch intermittent irregularity; do not rely on an automated cuff reading for rhythm.

interpretation.positive_finding: An irregularly irregular pulse is a sensitive screen (92-94%) for atrial fibrillation but only moderately specific (72-82%); frequent ectopy, sinus arrhythmia and multifocal atrial tachycardia mimic it, so a 12-lead ECG is mandatory to confirm.
interpretation.negative_finding: A regular pulse over 30-60 s makes sustained atrial fibrillation unlikely (LR- ~0.10), though paroxysmal AF and AF with rapid rates or a regularized ventricular response can be missed.
interpretation.pitfalls: Rapid AF can feel regular; a pulse deficit means the radial rate underestimates the heart rate; a single short palpation misses paroxysmal AF; irregularity does not distinguish AF from flutter with variable block.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: obtain a 12-lead ECG now and, if AF, assess rate, hemodynamics, stroke risk and anticoagulation; negative: AF becomes an unlikely explanation for the symptom at this moment.

estimates.population: 3 studies, 2385 adults (mostly elderly primary-care/screening and hospital populations) undergoing pulse palpation compared with ECG
estimates.quote: Pooled sensitivity was 94% (95% confidence interval [CI], 84%-97%) and pooled specificity was 72% (95% CI, 69%-75%). The pooled positive likelihood ratio was 3.39
estimates.location: Abstract, Results (LR- 0.10 in the following abstract sentence)

estimates.target_condition: Atrial fibrillation (12-lead ECG-diagnosed), detected by pulse palpation
estimates.population: 6 pulse-palpation interventions within a 21-study, 15,129-assessment meta-analysis; predominantly primary-care/community AF screening in older adults
estimates.location: Abstract, Results; also Results text, PMC4952027 full text

sources.citation: Cooke G, Doust J, Sanders S. Is pulse palpation helpful in detecting atrial fibrillation? A systematic review. J Fam Pract. 2006;55(2):130-134.

Taggar JS, Coleman T, Lewis S, Heneghan C, Jones M. Accuracy of methods for detecting an irregular pulse and suspected atrial fibrillation: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Eur J Prev Cardiol. 2016;23(12):1330-1338.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use pulse palpation instead of an ECG when a rhythm diagnosis will change management (anticoagulation, cardioversion, rate control), or in a hemodynamically unstable patient.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Irregular pulse with hypotension, chest pain, heart failure, or a new neurological deficit needs immediate ECG and monitored care; suspected AF plus stroke symptoms is a time-critical stroke pathway.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Palpation agreement is fair to moderate; specificity is the weak point, with ectopy commonly over-called as AF. Non-12-lead ECG devices and oscillometric AF-detecting BP monitors outperform palpation for specificity.

extraction_notes: Sens/spec entered as percent (Taggar quote preserves decimal fractions). Both estimates are pooled from screening-type populations comparing palpation with ECG; performance in symptomatic ED patients with palpitations/syncope was not separately reported and prevalence in the target inpatient population will differ. Cooke 2006 abstract gives LR+ 3.39 and LR- 0.10 without CIs; the quoted sentence contains sens/spec/LR+ and the LR- appears in the immediately following sentence at the same location. Taggar 2016 full text (PMC4952027) also reports a sensitivity-analysis pulse-palpation estimate of 0.93 (0.86-0.97)/0.81 (0.76-0.85), not entered separately. PubMed lists the Taggar article year as 2017 in one field; print citation is 2016;23(12):1330.
